I'll execute the full 10-phase accessibility design review protocol on this accordion component. --- ## Phase 0 — Consume Test Evidence No test evidence provided (no axe-core results, no Playwright keyboard tests, no VSR logs). Proceeding with source-code-only analysis. Claims about dynamic behavior will note where measurement would strengthen confidence. --- ## Phase 1 — Pre-commitment Predictions For a disclosure/accordion widget, I predict: 1. **Missing `role="region"` on panels** — The fixture name itself hints at this. Panels without region role won't be announced as navigable landmarks when expanded. 2. **Missing `aria-labelledby` on panels** — Without it, screen readers can't associate panel content with its trigger button. 3. **No heading semantics** — WAI-ARIA APG Disclosure pattern expects buttons to be wrapped in or paired with headings (`

`, `

`). Standalone buttons break the expected information hierarchy. 4. **Default-expanded first item may confuse** — `useState(0)` opens the first panel on mount. This is a design choice, but without an announcement, screen reader users land on already-expanded content with no context. 5. **No arrow key navigation between triggers** — Single-expand accordions often benefit from arrow keys to jump between items without tabbing through every page element. --- ## Phase 2 — Semantic HTML Audit | Check | Status | Notes | |-------|--------|-------| | Native `

``` **Confidence:** HIGH ### 3. No arrow key navigation between triggers — keyboard efficiency degraded **Evidence:** `BuggyAccordion.jsx:18` — button has only `onClick`, no `onKeyDown` handler for Arrow Up/Down. **User group impacted:** Keyboard-only users **Expected behavior:** Per WAI-ARIA APG Disclosure Widgets, grouped disclosure elements should support Arrow Up/Down to move focus between triggers. This allows keyboard users to navigate within the accordion without Tabbing through all page elements. WCAG 2.1.1 (Keyboard). **Fix:** Add `onKeyDown` handler: ```jsx const handleKeyDown = (e, index) => { if (e.key === 'ArrowDown') { e.preventDefault(); const nextIndex = (index + 1) % items.length; document.getElementById(`trigger-${nextIndex}`)?.focus(); } else if (e.key === 'ArrowUp') { e.preventDefault(); const prevIndex = (index - 1 + items.length) % items.length; document.getElementById(`trigger-${prevIndex}`)?.focus(); } }; ``` **Confidence:** HIGH --- ## Minor Findings (friction but workaround exists) - **Default-expanded first item has no announcement** — `useState(0)` opens panel 0 on mount. A screen reader user landing on the accordion sees expanded content without context. Mitigated by: user can still Tab through and discover structure. Consider adding an `aria-live="polite"` region that announces "Accordion loaded, [title] expanded" on mount, or change default to `-1` (all collapsed). --- ## Enhancements (best practice not met) - **Outer accordion container has no accessible label** — `
` could benefit from `role="group"` and `aria-label="Frequently asked questions"` (or context-appropriate label) to orient screen reader users to the widget's purpose. - **Consider `aria-pressed` alternative for single-expand** — While `aria-expanded` is correct per APG, some teams prefer explicit "one open at a time" semantics via radio-group pattern. Not required, but worth noting for design system consistency. --- ## What's Missing (gaps, unhandled edge cases) 1. **No button IDs for `aria-labelledby` association** — Buttons lack `id` attributes, making it impossible to link panels back to triggers even if `aria-labelledby` were added. 2. **No keyboard shortcut documentation** — If arrow keys are added, there's no visible or ARIA-exposed hint that they're available. Consider adding `aria-keyshortcuts="ArrowUp ArrowDown"` (WCAG 4.1.2) or a visually-hidden instruction note. 3. **No handling for empty `items` array** — If `items.length === 0`, the accordion renders an empty `
` with no content and no announcement. Consider rendering a fallback message or hiding the container entirely. 4. **No `aria-live` region for dynamic state changes** — When panels expand/collapse, there's no live region announcing the change. For most accordions this is acceptable (the button's `aria-expanded` change is sufficient), but if content is complex or lengthy, a polite announcement improves orientation. --- ## Multi-Perspective Notes - **Screen reader user:** CRITICAL gap. Panels have no region role and no label association. Expanding a panel reveals unstructured text with no programmatic link to the trigger. Heading navigation shortcuts are useless because no headings exist. The disclosure interaction model is broken for AT users. - **Keyboard-only user:** MAJOR gap. Functional with Tab/Enter/Space, but no arrow key navigation between triggers. Inefficient for long accordions where users must Tab through intervening page content to reach the next item. - **Low vision user:** No issues detected in markup. Button targets are standard interactive elements. Contrast and zoom concerns are CSS-level, not present in this review scope. - **Cognitive accessibility:** Clear +/- indicators, single-expand reduces cognitive load. No timeouts or destructive actions. Error handling N/A for this component. --- ## Verdict Justification **REVISE** because the ARIA pattern is incomplete at a structural level. The visible attributes (`aria-expanded`, `aria-controls`) are correct, but the assistive technology relationship layer (`role="region"`, `aria-labelledby`, heading semantics) is absent. This means screen reader users cannot associate panel content with its trigger — a fundamental breakdown of the disclosure interaction model. To upgrade to **ACCEPT-WITH-RESERVATIONS**, the developer must: 1. Add `role="region"` and `aria-labelledby` to all panels (CRITICAL fix) 2. Wrap buttons in heading elements or add adjacent headings (MAJOR fix) 3. Add button IDs to enable the labeling association Arrow key navigation and mount announcements are recommended but not blocking for acceptance. --- ## Open Questions (unscored) - Is the default-expanded first item (`useState(0)`) intentional product behavior, or should all items start collapsed (`useState(-1)`)? This affects whether a mount announcement is needed. - Are there CSS transitions/animations on panel expand/collapse? If so, `prefers-reduced-motion` handling should be reviewed separately. - Is this accordion used in a context where a landmark role (`role="group"` with label) on the container would help orient screen reader users to the section's purpose?
